claims.text: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts typically use aggregated platinum-group metals with relatively low atom efficiency.
Mechanochemical synthesis can produce atomically dispersed Pd single atoms on a high-entropy fluorite oxide support.
The high-entropy composition of the fluorite oxide stabilizes atomically dispersed Pd sites.
The high-entropy fluorite oxide support resists Pd sintering.
Atomic dispersion of Pd maximizes the exposure of catalytically active Pd sites.
Greater exposure of single-atom Pd sites enhances turnover frequency.
The high-entropy matrix thermally and chemically stabilizes single-atom Pd sites.
Stabilization of single-atom Pd sites mitigates catalyst deactivation.
Single-atom Pd on HEFO can maintain or enhance catalytic performance while reducing total platinum-group-metal consumption.
Single-atom Pd on HEFO will provide higher turnover frequency than conventional aggregated PGM catalysts.
Single-atom Pd on HEFO will retain higher catalytic conversion after thermal aging than conventional aggregated PGM catalysts.
Single-atom Pd on HEFO will have a longer catalyst lifetime than conventional aggregated PGM catalysts.
The predicted performance can be achieved with a lower palladium loading than the PGM loading used in platinum-based systems.
Sintering and low atom efficiency compromise the activity and durability of conventional aggregated-PGM automotive catalysts.
The anticipated performance gains may depend on exhaust composition, operating-temperature fluctuations, and reproducibility of the synthesis.
